lxc_aca4de1942f428e6.text: Japanese comics called manga are read by millions of people around the world.

lxc_0f5d31443911868c.text: They began hundreds of years ago and changed a lot over time.

lxc_8faff5cfea3d6c94.text: You will learn where manga started, how it grew, who reads it, and how you can read it today.

lxc_3c196599b9d52f08.text: These old works are manga's early illustrated roots.

lxc_b1c3ac8149d79b4a.text: Manga has very old roots in Japan.

lxc_76e53a64aca0f426.text: Around the year 1200, artists drew funny animal pictures on long paper scrolls.

lxc_054a837a96ef5c57.text: These scrolls are called Chōjū-giga, which means 'animal caricatures.'

lxc_4350d4e11b43d2d7.text: Frogs and rabbits wrestle and play like humans.

lxc_3c8f538bf86bab15.text: Many people call Chōjū-giga the oldest manga.

lxc_b4f083d46ac8fa8e.text: About 600 years later, an artist named Katsushika Hokusai used the word 'manga' for the first time.

lxc_b156dba2bfc53053.text: In 1814, he published a book of sketches called Hokusai Manga.

lxc_7ad60b7c39cb258d.text: The book showed people, animals, plants, and landscapes.

lxc_ac549bfa3526954f.text: Hokusai drew over 3,000 pictures across 15 volumes.

lxc_035c2366b8fd0126.text: His work showed that a series of pictures could tell many ideas together.

lxc_b0ab1e44b36de036.text: This modern manga development changed picture stories in Japan.

lxc_147f423f052c6a63.text: Modern manga began after World War Two.

lxc_681d601d6a9ba212.text: American comic books came to Japan, and Japanese artists saw a new way to tell stories.

lxc_01697d521b3b827e.text: Osamu Tezuka published New Treasure Island in 1947.

lxc_0db66c30ddef01fb.text: This comic book told an adventure story with fast camera-like angles, close-up faces, and action scenes.

lxc_bbcf2c2e75a2b3dd.text: Many other artists copied Tezuka's style.

lxc_01efa91872575458.text: He later created Astro Boy, a story about a robot boy, which also became a famous anime.

lxc_f1dd6a69841b90c6.text: Tezuka is often called 'the God of Manga.'

lxc_02e6b32004ca49fc.text: His work set the visual style that most people think of as manga today.

lxc_0ab575e8256dce99.text: New kinds of stories helped manga reach wide manga audiences.

lxc_8637a7d5b66f8861.text: Not everyone wants the same story.

lxc_8f017f14e038f509.text: Manga publishers learned this and made different types for different readers.

lxc_3098d9710a088825.text: In the 1950s and 1960s, some artists wanted more serious stories for adults.

lxc_218387922338e5e7.text: They created a style called gekiga, which means 'dramatic pictures.'

lxc_5855e08846dee818.text: Gekiga stories showed real life problems, crime, and social issues.

lxc_511b2c4fd730526a.text: At the same time, publishers started making manga for girls.

lxc_ae86baacedf20a32.text: This type is called shōjo manga.

lxc_1d6e4ab1ca298583.text: Shōjo stories focused on feelings, friendships, and romance.

lxc_b2bb75612ddd4f40.text: The pictures used large expressive eyes and soft lines.

lxc_c9afda2df6363fa0.text: Today, there is manga for children, teenagers, men, women, and older adults.

lxc_a0722b44f4854da0.text: Each type has its own name and its own magazine.

lxc_0987e76a93c8af8f.text: This is one reason why manga became so popular — almost everyone can find a story made for them.

lxc_d9736d58131a2850.text: Official online services now give manga global digital reach.

lxc_3ad29de640f23dff.text: Manga moved from Japan to the whole world, first through anime and then through digital technology.

lxc_344351b738e6f506.text: When Astro Boy became a TV anime in 1963, international audiences discovered Tezuka's characters.

lxc_63ee7de4e4044411.text: Later, publishers began translating manga into English, French, Spanish, and many other languages.

lxc_9fc835d6b4a289cc.text: Now readers can use digital platforms to read manga online.

lxc_95c2b80492e85084.text: Some publishers release new chapters at the same time in Japan and in other countries.

lxc_e5b6384abf619436.text: This is called a simultaneous release.
